name: Kienböck Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical and radiological findings

criteria.description: Chronic dorsal wrist pain localized to the lunate region
Radiographic evidence of lunate sclerosis, fragmentation, or collapse
MRI findings consistent with lunate avascular necrosis including decreased signal intensity on T1-weighted images
Reduced wrist range of motion, especially extension and flexion
Absence of significant preceding wrist trauma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic dorsal wrist pain with radiographic or MRI evidence of lunate avascular necrosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; biopsy rarely required.

laboratory: No specific laboratory abnormalities; inflammatory markers usually normal
imaging: X-ray showing lunate sclerosis, fragmentation, or collapse
MRI demonstrating decreased T1 signal intensity and variable T2 signal in lunate
CT scan may show lunate fragmentation and carpal alignment
other: Histopathology shows avascular necrosis of lunate bone

distinguishingFeatures: Localized tenderness over scaphoid rather than lunate
Positive rheumatoid factor or anti-CCP antibodies
Joint space narrowing and erosions on imaging
Degenerative changes in multiple wrist joints
Absence of lunate avascular necrosis on imaging

redFlags: Severe persistent pain unresponsive to conservative treatment
references: Linscheid RL, Dobyns JH. Kienböck's disease: current concepts. J Hand Surg Am. 1980;5(3):272-283.
Watson HK, Ballet FL. The SLAC wrist: scapholunate advanced collapse pattern of degenerative arthritis. J Hand Surg Am. 1984;9(3):358-365.
